scope: Alabama (7), Mississippi (4), Louisiana (6) - check for map changes after Louisiana v. Callais and the switch to closed primaries; South Carolina (7), Tennessee (9)
method_notes: Results: NBC News district pages (AP data, NBC Decision Desk), read ~10:59-11:06 AM ET Nov 4; percentages only (NBC per-candidate vote cells displayed 0). other_pct = 100 - dem_pct - rep_pct (residual). Calls: NBC shows no per-race call marker in fetched text; NBC house-results page lists uncalled counts AL 0, MS 0, LA 2, SC 2, TN 2, and the six races with NBC 'would need X% of remaining vote' text (TN-4, TN-9, SC-1, SC-2, LA-5, LA-6) match those counts exactly, so all other races are recorded as called by NBC (inferred). Baselines: unless noted, pres2024_margin = NBC margin minus NBC's stated 'shifted X points toward Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential election' figure, i.e. derived, not independently reported; NBC's shift may be two-party based; cross-checked against Wikipedia/Dave's Redistricting rounded figures where available. overperformance_vs_pres2024 therefore equals NBC's stated shift in those rows. Maps: AL redrew districts 1, 2, 6, 7 in May 2026 after Louisiana v. Callais (SCOTUS allowed use June 2); LA enacted SB 121 (May 29, 2026) eliminating one of two Black-plurality Democratic seats and moved House races to a Nov 3 jungle primary (runoff Dec 12) - not a closed primary; TN enacted HB 7003 (May 7, 2026) cracking Memphis (TN-9); SC House passed a VRA-redraw but SC Senate did not advance it, old map stands; MS map unchanged.
